newsitem.title: CANADA: Bid to delay Sable Island hearings rejected.
newsitem.headline: Bid to delay Sable Island hearings rejected.

text.p: Regulators rejected a bid by environmentalists to adjourn hearings on the (C)$3 billion Sable Island Offshore Energy Project, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

The National Energy Board panel ruled that Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien did not taint the hearings with comments last year favoring a plan to ship the natural gas on a pipeline route through Quebec, said NEB spokesman Edward Sampson.

The panel chairman Robert Fournier also rejected claims by the Ecology Action Centre that two of the panel's five members had a potential conflict of interest because they had once worked for companies involved in the hearings.

The panel is reviewing the viability of drilling for gas in the Atlantic Ocean 200 km east of Nova Scotia. It is believed to be one of North America's largest undeveloped gas deposits with reserves of 3 trillion cubic feet.
The project is lead by Mobil Oil Canada and includes Shell Canada Ltd, Imperial Oil Ltd and Nova Scotia Resources Ltd.

The proposal also calls for constructing the Maritimes and Northeast Pipeline that would ship the gas through Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Maine to southern New England. Martimes and Northeast will be owned by Mobil, Westcoast Energy Inc and PanEnergy Corp.

The NEB panel will hear preliminary evidence from the competing Trans-Quebec and Maritimes pipeline (TQM) proposal that calls for shipping the gas to Montreal before it goes to the U.S. TQM is owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP.

The hearings will continue until late May when the panel will decide if it needs more evidence on the pipeline issue. The NEB is expected to issue a recommendation to the federal government in early fall. If approved, the gas could be flowing by November, 1999.
